text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.4% today as oil markets reacted sharply to escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East. Iran intensified attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, sending U.S. crude prices up sharply and Brent crude to $110 per barrel. For a major oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher oil prices directly boost profitability — the company benefits when the commodity it extracts and sells commands a higher price.

The stock's 15.6% surge over two weeks reflects a broader shift in oil market expectations. Analysts have noted that physical delivery costs — what it actually takes to get oil from wellhead to buyer — add roughly $38 per barrel on top of the headline price, suggesting the true economic value of oil is well above current market quotes. As geopolitical risk persists and tanker rates remain elevated, investors are repricing energy stocks higher.
